claims: Aurora borealis is also known as northern lights.
Aurora borealis are lights in the night sky caused by solar particles colliding with Earth’s magnetic field and atmosphere.
Solar winds (charged particles) interact with Earth's magnetic field, causing gas atoms in the atmosphere to glow.
Aurora borealis are primarily visible in high-latitude regions near the Arctic.
Aurora borealis are primarily visible from August to April.
Aurora borealis displays appear as green, pink, or red.
Aurora borealis are most active between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m.
Aurora borealis are best viewed in high-latitude areas like Alaska, Canada, Iceland, Norway.
Aurora borealis can be viewed further south during strong geomagnetic storms.
The best time to view aurora borealis is late fall to early spring (August–April), specifically around midnight.
Green is the most common color of aurora borealis.
Aurora borealis colors can include pink, red, yellow, blue, and violet depending on the gas involved and altitude.
Aurora borealis typically occur 80 to 500 km above Earth's surface.
Aurora borealis can appear as curtains, rays, arcs, and coronal patches.
According to recent forecasts, a strong geomagnetic storm may allow the northern lights to be visible as far south as the northern United States in late March/early April 2026.
